**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/21 (Sun) 18:53  
[FACT] User is working on a model build.  
[PREFERENCE] User is trying to decide on a weathering technique for a military aircraft model.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Weathering can enhance a model, especially military aircraft.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] General tips for achieving a realistic worn look on a military aircraft model include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Study reference images of the real aircraft in various conditions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Understand the environment the aircraft faced.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Start with a good base coat.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Use a variety of weathering products: washes, drybrushing, chalks, pastels, enamel, or acrylic paints.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Focus on high-wear areas like leading edges, engine intakes, landing gear, cockpit frames, and areas around panel lines.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Build up weathering gradually in layers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Blend weathering effects using a soft brush or blending stump.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Avoid over-weathering to maintain a realistic appearance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Add subtle streaks and stains to simulate leaks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. Practice and experiment with techniques.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 11. Continuously refer to reference images for accuracy.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips specific to military aircraft include considering the age and maintenance history, distinctive weathering patterns, and weathering the underside of the model.  
[PREFERENCE] User is working on a Revell 1/48 F-15E Strike Eagle kit.  
[PREFERENCE] User is thinking of using a mix of Vallejo Model Air paints and enamel washes for weathering.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for blending washes with acrylic paints include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Choose the right wash that complements the Vallejo Model Air colors.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Thin washes with a solvent for a subtle effect.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Apply washes to recessed areas for depth.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Use a "glaze" technique to blend washes with base colors.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Blend with a wet brush to merge the two mediums.
